chunks: Aban, from Al-Wasiti, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah created Adam (peace be upon him) from water and clay, so the keenness/desire of the son of Adam is in water and clay; and He created Hawwa from Adam, so the keenness/desire of women is in men, therefore fortify/protect them in the houses.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological basis for keeping women in the houses according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the physical origin of humanity to their psychological inclinations, noting that men’s desire for water and clay mirrors Adam’s creation, while women’s desire for men reflects Hawwa’s origin from him. This hadith provides the metaphysical basis for the concept of 'hissan' (fortification/protection) within the domestic sphere, a key theme in al-Kafi regarding marital stability and female modesty in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores the complementary nature of genders and the structural role of the home in preserving spiritual and social order.

en.hubeali: (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created Adam<sup>as</sup> from the water and the clay, so the keenness of the son of Adam<sup>as</sup> is in the water and the clay; and Created Hawwa<sup>as</sup> for Adam<sup>as</sup>, so the keenness of the women is in the men, therefore fortify them in the houses’.
en.sarwar: 4. Aban has narrated from al-Wasitiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Allah created Adam from water and clay so the ambition of the sons of Adam is in water and clay. He created Eve from Adam so the ambition of women is for men and their fortress is in the houses.’”
